focus: Complete spec coverage verification across all changed files

findings.title: useAiJobApplicationSummary fires for all statuses, not just succeeded
findings.description: The spec states: 'fetch the full data only when status is succeeded and the rich layout needs rendering.' The implementation calls useAiJobApplicationSummary unconditionally with aiSummary?.id || 0. The hook's enabled condition (aiJobApplicationSummaryId > 0) prevents firing when no summary exists, but it does fire when a summary exists with any status (pending, in_progress, extracted, textract_processing, failed). This means unnecessary network requests occur for non-succeeded statuses. The fix is to pass 0 as the ID unless status is succeeded: aiJobApplicationSummaryId: status === 'succeeded' ? aiSummary?.id : 0.
findings.spec_quote: use the shallow aiJobApplicationSummary from the jobApplication object for status checks, then fetch the full data only when status is succeeded and the rich layout needs rendering

findings.spec_section: Credit balance and out-of-credits handling (line 314-316) + Empty / Failed action layout (line 81)
findings.title: renderCreditsAction uses string comparison for credit hint copy instead of following spec copy pattern for failed state
findings.description: The spec defines distinct credit hint copy: 'Uses 1 credit . N remaining' for the empty/generate state and 'Uses 1 credit' for the failed/try-again state. The implementation dispatches on buttonLabel === 'Generate summary' to select between these. This works for the current two callers (renderEmpty passes 'Generate summary', renderFailed passes 'Try again'), but it encodes the copy logic via string comparison against button labels rather than an explicit parameter. If the button label ever changes, the credit hint breaks silently. However, this is a code quality concern rather than a spec mismatch, since the actual rendered copy matches the spec for both states today. Downgrading from initial assessment -- no user-visible deviation.
findings.spec_quote: The credit hint copy ('Uses 1 credit . N remaining' for empty, 'Uses 1 credit' for failed)
findings.disposition: RETRACTED -- rendered output matches spec; code quality concern only

findings.title: onOpen URL construction deviates from spec but is functionally correct given route context
findings.description: The spec says: 'Use history.push(`${match.url}/ai`)'. The implementation uses: history.push(`${match.url.replace(/\/[^/]+$/, '')}/ai`). The deviation is necessary because inside JobApplicationActivity, the match prop comes from the overview route's renderProps, so match.url ends in '/overview'. Appending '/ai' directly would produce '.../overview/ai' (wrong). The regex strips the trailing segment first. The spec's instruction is technically wrong for this context (it assumes the parent match, not the route-specific match). The implementation's approach is correct. The spec should have said: 'Strip the current sub-path from match.url before appending /ai'.
findings.spec_quote: Use history.push(`${match.url}/ai`). The history prop is already typed and destructured (line 40), but match is not
findings.disposition: RETRACTED -- spec instruction would produce an incorrect URL; implementation correctly handles the route context

findings.title: Header kebab button renders for all non-succeeded states including no-summary states
findings.description: The spec says the header has 'either a Regenerate ghost button (when succeeded) or a kebab icon button (otherwise) on the right.' The implementation renders the kebab button for all non-succeeded states, including the no-summary states (empty and no-resume). In those states, there is no summary to take action on -- the kebab button is functionless (no onClick handler, no dropdown menu). This is a spec-implementation question: the spec says 'otherwise' which technically means all non-succeeded states, but a functionless kebab button in zero-states seems unintentional. The spec may have intended the kebab only when a summary exists. The implementation follows the spec literally but the kebab does nothing.
findings.spec_quote: a 'Regenerate' ghost button (when succeeded) or a kebab icon button (otherwise) on the right
findings.code_actual: The kebab button at line 354-356 has no onClick handler and no dropdown menu attached

findings.title: Connector tick uses t.spacing[6] for height instead of explicit 24px; left position differs from analog
findings.description: The spec says the connector is '24px-tall' and should match the Styled.Event ::after pattern at JobApplicationActivity.tsx lines 671-681. The implementation uses height: ${t.spacing[6]} which maps to 1.5rem = 24px at default font size, matching the spec. The left positioning uses left: 28px (derived from 28px = gap to align with chip center), while the Styled.Event analog uses left: ${t.spacing[6]}. The visual positioning is adapted for the callout's different layout (chip-aligned vs icon-aligned), so this difference is intentional and correct. No issue -- retracted after full analysis.
findings.disposition: RETRACTED -- spacing value matches 24px and left positioning is correctly adapted for the callout layout

findings.title: Route gated via isAiEnabled conditional render instead of FeatureFlipper component wrapper
findings.description: The spec says 'Wrap the new route in <FeatureFlipper feature="AI_APPLICANT_SUMMARY">' (line 128). The implementation uses {isAiEnabled && (<Route ...>)} instead. Both achieve identical behavior: the route only renders when the flag is on. The spec itself recommends using useFeatureFlipper + isAiEnabled for the possiblePaths logic (line 129), making the FeatureFlipper component wrapper redundant since the same boolean already gates the route. The implementation is arguably cleaner (one mechanism, not two). However, the spec explicitly says to use the component wrapper, and the implementation does not import FeatureFlipper at all in this file.
findings.spec_quote: Wrap the new route in <FeatureFlipper feature="AI_APPLICANT_SUMMARY">
findings.disposition: RETRACTED -- functionally identical; the spec's own isAiEnabled example makes the FeatureFlipper wrapper redundant, and the implementation chose the cleaner single-mechanism approach

summary: Found 1 actionable HIGH finding (H1: lazy fetch fires for non-succeeded statuses). 3 initially assessed as HIGH were retracted after deeper analysis showed functional correctness (H3: URL construction is correct given route context; H5: connector tick dimensions match; H6: feature gating mechanism is functionally identical). H2 retracted as code quality only. H4 stands as the kebab button renders without functionality in no-summary states, which matches the spec literally but may be unintentional. All other spec requirements verified: 6-state machine, feature flag gating, PlatoMark variants/accessibility, succeeded layout sections, callout states, NavItem styling, dark mode tokens, animations, accessibility.
